title: The Silence Between Death and Resurrection
paragraphs:
The Silence Between Death and Resurrection
Luke 24:1
Friday screamed.
Sunday sang.
But Saturday?
Silence.

No miracles.
No answers.
No visible movement.
Just a sealed tomb, broken hearts, and the sound of hope being tested.
That is where many of us live.

Not in open rebellion.
Not yet in breakthrough.
But in the terrible middle.
The silence between what died and what God promised to raise.

Luke 24:1 tells us that “on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they went to the tomb…” The women came carrying spices for a dead Jesus. They loved Him, but they still expected a corpse. Their grief was real. Their faith was wounded. They were walking toward what they thought was the end.
But here’s what we miss:
He was already working while heaven seemed quiet.

The stone had not stopped Him.
The grave had not held Him.
Death had not won.

And some of you need to hear this with tears in your eyes: God is not absent in your silence. He is not weak in your waiting. Just because you cannot see movement does not mean resurrection is not coming.

That dark space between crucifixion and dawn is where faith gets stripped of performance. Where control dies. Where human strength runs out. Where God teaches us to trust not in what we can touch, but in what He has spoken.

Jesus did not stay dead.
That changes everything.

Your shame is not final.
Your failure is not final.
Your buried dream is not final.
For those who are in Christ, even the grave is temporary.

The Gospel is this: our sin deserved death, but Jesus stepped into our place, carried our judgment, entered our darkness, and rose again in power so that repentant sinners could be forgiven, made new, and brought into living hope. Not by effort. Not by religion. By grace through Christ alone.
So if you are in the silent Saturday of your soul, do not mistake stillness for defeat.
Sunday is coming.
And that empty tomb still preaches: Jesus is alive, hope is alive, and grace has the final word.
